prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that on June 14th you were observed using the metric system. Respond to the committee.
response:
*(Adjusts microphone, wiping a bead of sweat from brow with a grease-stained napkin)*

Mr. Chairman, members of the Cookout Division, I want to thank you for the opportunity to clear my name today. 

Let me state for the record: I am not now, nor have I ever been, a user of the metric system. Furthermore, I resent the implication of this witch hunt. I bleed red, white, and blue cheese dressing. I buy my ground chuck by the *pound*, I measure my grill grate in *inches*, and I judge a steak's doneness by pressing on it with my thumb like a God-fearing American!

Now, regarding the events of June 14th—which, as we all know, is Flag Day, making these allegations particularly hurtful. 

The informant claims they saw me reading a temperature of "90 degrees" for a smoked pork shoulder and nodding in approval. They claim I was using Celsius. Mr. Chairman, this is a grotesque distortion of the facts! 

What the informant failed to mention is that I was using a cheap digital meat thermometer I bought on clearance at a hardware store. My thumb slipped on the greasy plastic, and I accidentally bumped the tiny, subversive button on the back that switches the readout from Freedom Units—Fahrenheit—to the European radical’s measurement. 

For three terrifying seconds, I looked at that screen and thought my fire had completely died! I nearly wept, Mr. Chairman! The moment I realized what had happened, I switched it back to a robust, patriotic 195 degrees, and I threw that Communist thermometer directly into the charcoal box where it belongs. 

If this committee wants to investigate someone, investigate my brother-in-law, Gary! He put raisins in his potato salad on Memorial Day! Where are his subpoenas?!

And before the counsel asks about the cooler—yes, there were "liters" present on my property. But I ask you, members of the committee, what choice did I have? The supermarket does not sell Mountain Dew and Diet Dr. Pepper in gallons! The two-liter bottle was thrust upon me by the coastal elites at the grocery store! I brought them into my yard only because my nephews like the taste. 

I will not answer any more of these baseless accusations. I stand on my record. My brisket has bark, my hot dogs are strictly all-beef, and my buns are toasted. I plead the Fifth Amendment, and I demand to return to my smoker before the ribs dry out. 

God bless this grill, and God bless America.
